The structure of Ba2Mg12Si2 (reduced formula BaMg6Si) crystallizes in the tetragonal space group I-4m2 (No. 119), with 16 atoms per unit cell distributed over five independent Wyckoff orbits. Geometry-derived analysis identifies close-packed-like local arrangements: Ba and Si centers each have 12 geometric neighbors, while Mg centers show 12 neighbors in several distinct environments. The neighbor graph is three-dimensional and connected across all 16 sites. Validated polyhedron contacts reveal Mg-centered 12-vertex polyhedra sharing corners, edges, and faces, while Ba- and Mg-centered polyhedra share edges.
